351696.title: The leafless-graph upper-bound conjecture for edge metric dimension
351696.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Its **edge metric dimension** is denoted by $\mathrm{edim}(G)$, its **cyclomatic number** by $c(G)=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1$, and $L(G)$ is the sum of the excess numbers of threads hanging at vertices. A graph is **leafless** when its minimum degree satisfies $\delta(G)\geq2$.

**Leafless-graph upper-bound conjecture.** Every leafless graph satisfies

$$
\mathrm{edim}(G)\leq 2c(G)-1.
$$

The paper proves this decreased bound for leafless cacti and for graphs with minimum degree at least three. Together with the analogous vertex statement, it is proposed as the sharp replacement for the earlier bound involving $L(G)$; the general case remains open.

351726.title: The multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture for multiset-proper edge-labellings
351726.statement:

A graph is **nice** if none of its connected components is isomorphic to $K_2$, and let $\chi_{\rm M}(G)$ be the smallest $k\geq 1$ for which $G$ has an m-proper $k$-labelling, meaning an edge-labelling from $\{1,\dots,k\}$ whose incident-label multisets give different values at the ends of every edge.

**The multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture for multisets.** If $G$ is a nice graph, then

$$
\chi_{\rm M}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This is the multiset counterpart of the original 1-2-3 Conjecture, raised by Addario-Berry, Aldred, Dalal and Reed. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied material.

351953.title: Gang–Kim–Yoon's norm-curve vanishing conjecture for adjoint Reidemeister torsions
351953.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented compact hyperbolic $3$-manifold with a torus boundary. A **norm curve** is a one-dimensional component of the character variety on which every trace function is non-constant; write $X^{\mathrm{nor}}(M)$ for the set of all norm curves. For a slope $\gamma\in H_1(\partial M,\mathbb Z)$, let $\operatorname{tr}\rho(\gamma)$ be the trace of $\rho(\gamma)$ and let $\mathbb T_{M,\gamma}$ be the adjoint Reidemeister torsion. **Modified Gang–Kim–Yoon conjecture.** For generic $z\in\mathbb C$, 

$$
\sum_{\substack{[\rho]\in X^{\mathrm{nor}}(M)\\ \operatorname{tr}\rho(\gamma)=z}}\frac{1}{\mathbb T_{M,\gamma}}=0.
$$

The modification excludes extra character-variety components containing constant trace functions. The paper shows that this identity holds for all hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundles with tunnel number one, although its validity in the stated generality remains open.

351989.title: Continuous Zauner's conjecture for equiangular tight continuous frames
351989.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\{\tau_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Omega}$ be a continuous frame for the Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$. The frame is **$\gamma$-equiangular** if there exists $\gamma\geq 0$ such that

$$
|\langle\tau_\alpha,\tau_\beta\rangle|=\gamma,\qquad \forall\alpha,\beta\in\Omega,\ \alpha\neq\beta.
$$

It is **tight** if its frame operator is a scalar multiple of the identity. **Continuous Zauner's conjecture.** For a given measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a $\gamma$-equiangular tight continuous frame $\{\tau_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Omega}$ for $\mathbb{C}^d$ such that $\mu(\Omega)=d^2$. This is the continuous analogue of Zauner's conjecture for equiangular tight frames; the existence assertion is posed for every dimension and measure space, and its resolution is not supplied here.

such that

V\sim |x|+1,

where $1$ indicates the smallest normalized volume among the polytopes. 352000.title: Revised Vallentin conjecture for distance-regular graphs

Let $G$ be a distance-regular graph with diameter $d$, with eigenvalues $\theta_0>\theta_1>\cdots>\theta_d$ and cosine sequences $(w_0(\theta_j),\ldots,w_d(\theta_j))$ corresponding to the eigenvalues. $$

The maximum occurs at $r=d$ unless $G$ is antipodal. The paper proves this revised conjecture for diameter $3$ and gives partial results for diameter $4$.

352134.title: Ghosh–Győri–Martin–Paulos–Xiao conjecture on planar Turán numbers of cycles

$$
e(G)\le \frac{3(\ell-1)}{\ell}n-\frac{6(\ell+1)}{\ell}.
$$

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_{\ell})\le \frac{3(\ell-1)}{\ell}n-\frac{6(\ell+1)}{\ell}.
$$

This conjecture is the bound proposed by Ghosh, Győri, Martin, Paulos, and Xiao for planar Turán numbers of cycles of length at least seven; the paper disproves it.

352139.title: Set-wise intersection conjecture for perfect matchings
352139.statement:
Let $K_{2k}$ be the complete graph on $2k$ vertices. For $t\leq \lfloor k/2\rfloor$, two perfect matchings are **set-wise $t$-intersecting** if some $t$ edges in each matching cover the same set of vertices. A family is set-wise $t$-intersecting if every pair of its members is set-wise $t$-intersecting.

**Set-wise intersection conjecture.** For $k\geq 2t$, the largest set-wise $t$-intersecting family of perfect matchings in $K_{2k}$ has size

$$
(2t-1)!!(2k-2t-1)!!.
$$

Moreover, every maximum-size family is an orbit of the Young subgroup $Sym(2t)\times Sym(2k-2t)$.

This conjecture extends the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem from ordinary intersection to set-wise intersection. The paper proves the corresponding result for $t=2$; the cases $t\geq 3$ remain open.

352241.title: Infinite-family conjecture for non-Paley pseudo-Paley graphs
352241.statement:
For a prime $p\geq 3$, consider subsets $I\subset\{0,1,\ldots,p\}$ with $0\in I$ and $|I|=(p+1)/2$, and the associated graph $PP(p^4,p+1,I)$. Let $g$ be the primitive element used to define the cyclotomic classes. **Infinite-family conjecture.** For each prime $p\geq 3$, exactly

$$
\frac{p^2+3}{4}
$$

such subsets $I$ satisfy

$$
\omega\bigl(PP(p^4,p+1,I)\bigr)=p^2.
$$

Furthermore, in these graphs, every maximum clique containing $\{0,1\}$ is of the form

$$
\mathbb{F}_p\oplus a\mathbb{F}_p,

352283.title: Uniform Fitting-height conjecture for fixed-point-free automorphisms satisfying polynomial identities
352283.statement:
Let $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\setminus\{0\}$. An automorphism $\alpha$ of a finite group $G$ has **ordered identity** $f(x)$ if the corresponding identity in the group ring holds for $\alpha$; it is **fixed-point-free** if $C_G(\alpha)=1$. The **Fitting height** of a finite solvable group is the length of its Fitting series.

**Uniform Fitting-height conjecture.** For every $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\setminus\{0\}$, there exist integers $k(f(x))>0$ and $m(f(x))$ such that, whenever $G$ is a finite solvable group admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism $\alpha$ for which $f(x)$ is an ordered identity, the following hold: (a) the Fitting height of $G$ is at most $m(f(x))$; and (b) if $\gcd(|G|,k(f(x)))=1$, then the Fitting height of $G$ is at most the number of irreducible factors of $f(x)$.

The conjecture seeks a uniform bound depending only on the polynomial identity, with a sharper bound after excluding finitely many primes from $|G|$. It is motivated by results of Thompson, Berger, Turull and others on Fitting height under fixed-point-free automorphisms, but the stated uniform bounds are presented here as a conjecture.
